subject: accountancy
title: Sacrificing and gaining ratios
explanation: A partner's sacrifice is the old share minus the new share; a gain is the new share minus the old share. Work each continuing partner's change out separately, with a common denominator. The old ratio is the sacrificing ratio only when the incoming partner takes the share from the old partners in their old ratio.
workedContrast: J and K share 2:1. L joins and J, K and L share equally. J goes from 2/3 to 1/3, a sacrifice of 1/3. K goes from 1/3 to 1/3: no sacrifice at all. Using the old ratio, 2:1, would wrongly make K give something up.

explanations.general: Your answers pointed in different directions, so we will not label one reasoning gap. Start from the definition: sacrifice = old share − new share, gain = new share − old share, worked out for each partner separately.
explanations.secure: Two different scenarios showed you applying the distinction correctly. One short step, then fresh checks on question families you have not seen.
explanations.direction_reversed: Subtract in the direction of the change. Sacrifice = old share − new share, the part a partner gives up. Gain = new share − old share. A partner whose share falls has sacrificed; one whose share rises has gained.
explanations.old_ratio_default: The old ratio is a shortcut that holds only when the incoming partner takes the share from the old partners in their old ratio, or nothing else is stated. When a new ratio is given, compute old − new for each partner. Some partners may give up nothing, or even gain.
explanations.new_ratio_used: The new ratio describes shares after the change, not what each partner gave up. A partner with the larger new share may have sacrificed less, or gained. Compare each partner's old and new shares.

contrasts.general: J and K share 2:1. L joins and J, K and L share equally. J: 2/3 → 1/3, sacrifice 1/3. K: 1/3 → 1/3, no change. The sacrificing ratio is 1:0, not 2:1.
contrasts.secure: Check one partner at a time: write the old share and new share over a common denominator, subtract, then read the sign. Positive old − new is a sacrifice; negative is a gain.
contrasts.direction_reversed: S's share falls from 1/2 to 1/5: old − new = 3/10, so S sacrificed 3/10. Writing new − old gives −3/10, which reads as a gain and reverses the story.
contrasts.old_ratio_default: J and K share 2:1. L joins and all three share equally. The old ratio says J and K sacrifice 2:1. Working it out: J gives up 1/3, K gives up nothing. The stated new ratio overrides the shortcut.
contrasts.new_ratio_used: V and W share equally. X joins and the new ratio V:W:X is 2:1:1. The new ratio V:W is 2:1, yet V stays at 1/2 and gives up nothing, while W goes from 1/2 to 1/4, a sacrifice of 1/4.

probes.prompt: A and B share profits equally. C is admitted, and the new ratio of A, B and C is 1:3:1. Which statement about A and B is correct?
options: A sacrifices 3/10 and B gains 1/10
A and B sacrifice in their old ratio, 1:1
A and B sacrifice in the ratio 1:3
B sacrifices 1/10 and A gains 3/10

P sacrifices 3/10 and R gains 3/10; Q is unaffected
P, Q and R sacrifice in the new ratio, 2:3:5
